GAM follows the principle of "\textbf{just-in time (JIT) compilation}" where it focuses on creating optimized contexts for its client at runtime while keeping only simple but useful memory during the offline stage. Title: Pier: Efficient Large Language Model pretraining with Relaxed Global Communication Authors: Shuyuan Fan, Zhao Zhang Date: Sat Nov 22 00:29:04 2025 Global communication, such as all-reduce and allgather, is the prominent performance bottleneck in large language model (LLM) pretraining. To address this issue, we present Pier, an efficient and scalable optimizer with relaxed global communication. Pier is built upon DiLoCo, which leverages an inner optimizer within groups of processors and an outer optimizer that requires global communication. To preserve the convergence and model performance, Pier incorporates two key techniques for the outer optimizer: momentum warmup and momentum decay. Pier employs an efficient and scalable system architecture to enable complex parallelization strategies in LLM pretraining. We examine the model performance and runtime reduction of Pier using the GPT model family (e.g., small, medium, XL, and 7B) and the OpenWebText dataset with a suite of thirteen downstream tasks. With data parallel strategy, Pier speeds up GPT-2 XL training by up to 2.7x-3.7x on 256 NVIDIA A100 GPUs and 1.2x-1.9x on 64 GH200 Superchips, respectively, without degradation of validation loss or downstream task performance. The paper proposes General Agentic Memory (GAM), a dual-agent framework that replaces static, ahead-of-time (AOT) memory with just-in-time (JIT) “deep research” over a complete, paged store of history. ## General Agentic Memory via Deep Research: A Comprehensive Analysis ## Motivation and Problem Formulation The management and utilization of memory in LLM-based agents is a persistent challenge, especially as agents are deployed for tasks requiring long-horizon reasoning, intricate tool-use, and robust contextual recall. Traditional memory architectures largely rely on Ahead-of-Time (AOT) paradigms, which compress and precompute context into static, lightweight memories during the offline stage. This compression often leads to irrevocable information loss, undermining the ability to meet complex and ad-hoc information needs, and restricting adaptivity and generalization across domains. To overcome these limitations, the paper introduces General Agentic Memory (GAM), operationalized under a Just-in-Time (JIT) compilation principle. GAM combines long-term retention of complete historical context with dynamic, online deep research, targeting minimal memory loss and maximal adaptability. It directly formalizes the system objective as a cost-effectiveness optimization problem: create a context ^*∗ from task and history that is minimal in size yet maximal in downstream agent task performance. Image Figure 1: The memorizer generates lightweight summaries and a page-store of all historical data; the researcher retrieves and integrates information for each client request via deep research. ## Architecture: Memorizer and Researcher GAM consists of two tightly coupled LLM-based modules: ### 1. Memorizer The memorizer parses and processes the client agent's historical trajectory, segmenting it into sessions. For each session, it engages in: * Memorizing: Producing terse, structured memos highlighting essential session information. These snapshots are incrementally aggregated to update the lightweight memory. * Paging: Forming pages by decorating the session with headers containing key context cues, all stored in a universal page-store. This mechanism ensures lossless preservation and semantic coherence for subsequent retrieval operations. Image Figure 2: Memorizer prompt sequence illustrates the memory extraction process from each session. ### 2. Researcher The researcher operates during the online stage to satisfy new client requests by retrieving and integrating relevant information: * Planning: Analyzing the information need via chain-of-thought reasoning, subsequently generating search plans using available retrieval tools (embedding-based, BM25 keyword-based, and page-id direct search). * Searching: Executing planned search actions to retrieve pertinent pages, followed by iterative integration with previous results. * Reflection: Assessing adequacy of information; if incomplete, reformulating requests and re-invoking the search and integration cycle. Once sufficient, returning the synthesized context for downstream task execution. Image Figure 3: Researcher planning prompt illustrates the iterative reasoning and search tool selection. ### Paper to Video (Beta) No one has generated a video about this paper yet. The big idea: instead of trying to pack everything into memory ahead of time (which loses details), the AI keeps a full “library” of what happened and builds the exact context it needs on the spot, right when a question arrives. ## Overview The paper proposes General Agentic Memory (GAM), a dual-agent framework that replaces static, ahead-of-time (AOT) memory with just-in-time (JIT) “deep research” over a complete, paged store of history. GAM comprises: * A Memorizer that creates a lightweight, structured memory while storing full session content in a page-store with contextual headers. * A Researcher that plans, searches (embedding, BM25, ID-based), integrates, and reflects iteratively to generate optimized task-specific context at runtime.
